title: The Deductible Withheld From a Travel Protection Settlement
content:
The deductible withheld from a payment on a decided claim under the Travel Protection Plans depends on the
head the insurer decided and on how much of the plan's ceiling on the deductible withheld across one policy is
still unused. What remains of that ceiling is the plan's ceiling less the deductibles already withheld on the
policy's claim record, and is never less than nothing.

## The two figures each plan carries

| Plan | General deductible for each claim | Ceiling on deductible across one policy |
|---|---|---|
| Trip Basics Essential | 100 | 300 |
| Trip Basics Standard | 75 | 225 |
| TripGuard Plus | 50 | 150 |
| TripGuard Premier | 0 | 0 |
| Cancel For Any Reason Elite | 0 | 0 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Traveller | 50 | 150 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Executive | 0 | 0 |

Amounts are in USD.

## The four readings

1. Where the head decided is an emergency medical or dental treatment and what remains of the plan's ceiling on
   the deductible withheld across one policy is more than the plan's general deductible for each claim, the
   deductible withheld is the plan's medical deductible.
2. Where the head decided is damage to a hired vehicle and what remains of that ceiling is more than the plan's
   general deductible for each claim, the deductible withheld is the plan's rental vehicle damage deductible.
3. Where what remains of that ceiling is less than the plan's general deductible for each claim, the deductible
   withheld is only what remains of that ceiling.
4. In every other case the deductible withheld is the plan's general deductible for each claim.

The readings are taken in that order, so the first two govern where they hold, and the third answers only where
neither of them does.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

On a TripGuard Plus policy, whose general deductible for each claim is 50 and whose ceiling across one policy is
150, a claim record showing 50 already withheld leaves 100 of the ceiling. On an emergency medical head the first
reading holds, 100 being more than 50, and the deductible withheld is the plan's medical deductible. On a
baggage head the fourth reading holds and 50 is withheld. Where 120 had already been withheld, leaving 30, the
third reading holds on any head, 30 being less than 50, and only 30 is withheld. On a TripGuard Premier policy,
whose general deductible and ceiling are both 0, nothing remains of the ceiling and nothing is more than
nothing, so the fourth reading holds and the deductible withheld is 0.
